TASK: The quality inspector was walking from the inspection bench to the parts washer carrying a tote of samples. The task was routine scheduled work. Stage of the task: walking between areas. Method in effect: No written procedure exists for walking between these areas. No written procedure exists for this task. The object handled weighed 10 to 25 lb. Handling difficulty: bulky - hard to get arms around. It was held both hands and held against the body. PPE in use: safety glasses and steel toe boots. This matched the PPE specified for the task.

SEQUENCE: The event was witnessed by at least one other person. Immediately before the event: walking at normal pace along the main aisle with the tote held in both arms at chest height, looking ahead rather than down. Body position at the moment: carrying a load. At the moment of the event: the right foot contacted a patch of coolant on the aisle floor, the foot slid forward, balance was lost backwards, and the fall was taken onto the right hip and the outstretched right hand. Immediately after the event: the tote was dropped and the samples scattered, the inspector stayed on the floor for about a minute, and a passing operator called the team lead.

MECHANISM: Walking surface: sealed concrete. On or wrong with the surface: oil or coolant. Loss of footing: the right foot slid forward on the coolant, balance was lost backwards, and the fall was taken onto the right hip and the outstretched right hand. Footwear: slip resistant safety boots with worn soles. Point of contact: right hip, contacting the floor first. Force applied from below.

CONDITIONS: Difference from a normal run of this task: The coolant patch was new. Badge 448192 reported the same leak from the adjacent machine earlier in the shift. Conditions at the point of injury: a wet, oily or contaminated floor and poor or glaring lighting. Detail: The aisle light above this section has been out for about two weeks. The event occurred in the second half of the shift. Overtime was being worked that day. It happened within the first few seconds. The quality inspector had performed this task before. A known hazard, prior near miss, open action or risk assessment covers this task. Detail: A coolant leak on the adjacent machine was raised as a near miss about two weeks ago and the action to reseal the housing is still open. A guard, interlock, barrier or control was bypassed, missing, defeated or ineffective. Detail: Spill absorbent and cones are kept at the end of the aisle but the spill had not been marked or contained when first seen. Stop-work opportunity: The leak could have been reported and the aisle coned when it was first noticed earlier in the shift, but it was treated as a routine drip.

IMMEDIATE ACTIONS: At the scene, a cold pack was applied. This was given by a trained first aid responder. Notified: the team lead and EHS. This happened within a few minutes. Afterwards, the area was barriered off and a spill was contained. Work at the location stopped. The quality inspector was sent to an offsite occupational clinic for evaluation.
